name: paml
desc: Phylogenetic analyses of DNA or protein sequences using maximum likelihood
why: Maximum-likelihood phylogenetics on real DNA and protein sequences is genuine science you can run at home.

brief.what_it_is: PAML (Phylogenetic Analysis by Maximum Likelihood) is a package of command-line programs for phylogenetic analyses of DNA or protein sequences using maximum likelihood, maintained by Ziheng Yang and distributed under GPL v3. Its input is a sequence alignment plus a tree file and a plain-text control file, and its output is text: parameter estimates, likelihood values, and hypothesis-test results. The package has nine executables: baseml, basemlg, chi2, codeml, evolver, infinitesites, mcmctree, pamp, and yn00. The README says PAML is not for tree-building; you supply a tree from another program such as RAxML-NG, IQ-TREE, PAUP*, PHYLIP, or PhyML, and PAML estimates parameters and tests hypotheses on it.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents PAML as a tool for studying the evolutionary process by maximum likelihood, meaning estimating parameters and testing hypotheses on sequence data once trees are in hand. The README gives no separate problem statement.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It does say that users must format sequence data and tree files according to the Wiki's Data formatting section and set up control files, and that many user problems come from those inputs. Each program is run with its own control file, and the README points to the Wiki pages for BASEML, CODEML, MCMCtree and others for details.

commands_seen.context: Build step from the src directory of the source release; compiles all PAML programs.
Removes object files after compiling, per the install instructions in the releases notes.
Creates a bin directory, which the instructions say to add to PATH.

commands_seen.cmd: mv baseml basemlg chi2 codeml evolver infinitesites mcmctree pamp yn00 ../bin
commands_seen.context: Moves the compiled executables into the bin directory.
Test run suggested after install to confirm a program starts; the release notes list baseml, codeml and evolver.
Added in v4.10.10: merges MCMC sample files from independent MCMCtree runs saved in one directory into mcmc_combined.txt.
Added in v4.10.9: runs 1-D and 2-D density summaries on the MCMCtree output file (the mcmcfile path from the control file).
Manual compile line for the ds program, which the Makefile does not build.

brief.install_notes: The README points to the Installation wiki page with separate sections for Linux, macOS, and Windows 10 or later (via WSL), plus old compiled versions and the PAML-X GUI. The releases page says the source is ANSI C, built with make -f Makefile from the src directory, and that the compiled programs should then go into a bin directory on your PATH. The GitHub-generated source zip/tar.gz contains the current main branch (v4.10.9 at the time of the release page), not the legacy versions. Pre-v4.10 releases are bundled as one legacy release and are no longer maintained. Installation via brew is not described in the README.
brief.standout: PAML is a decades-old, widely cited package for codon and protein selection analyses and Bayesian divergence dating, and the author keeps the same software line alive with ongoing releases. Its documentation is migrating from PDF to a wiki, with an explicit FAQ and a rule to use the discussion group rather than GitHub issues for usage questions.
brief.status: Maintained. The latest release is 4.10.10, dated 29 Jan (the year is not shown in the page text I could read). The v4.10.9 release is dated 12 May, and v4.10.8 is dated 21 Apr. The releases page says the pre-v4.10 bundle is no longer actively maintained. The README says the Wiki is still under construction.
brief.caveats: Platform: the README lists UNIX, Linux, and Mac OS X for the ANSI C source and executables. Windows users are pointed to WSL, and old Windows executables exist only for legacy versions. The README says PAML is not for tree-making. The Wiki is still being written, and the PDF manuals are being migrated. The README asks that usage questions go to the Google discussion group and that GitHub issues be used only for compile or crash problems. Releases note an earlier arm64 Mac crash bug that was fixed in v4.10.8. The PAML-X GUI is described as no longer maintained and provided as-is. The license is GPL v3 per the README. The installed-program list from brew matches the nine executables in the README build instructions.
quotes: PAML (for Phylogenetic Analysis by Maximum Likelihood) is a package of programs for phylogenetic analyses of DNA or protein sequences using maximum likelihood.
PAML is not good for tree making, although it may be used to estimate parameters and test hypotheses to study the evolutionary process once you have reconstructed trees using other programs
Please, only raise an issue on this GitHub repository when you experience technical problems such as compiling issues, programs aborting or not running at all, etc.
